SMALL.note: concurrency=2/4 both ~32% SLOWER than concurrency=1 for this fixture. n=1 per condition (single live run each, per the pre-registered bounded-traffic design) - cannot statistically distinguish a genuine concurrency-caused effect from ordinary run-to-run variance (this benchmark's 9 runs share ONE persistent process-wide utils.rate_limiter token bucket; the SMALL/concurrency=1 run happened to run FIRST in sequence and its first call had rate_limit_wait_ms=0.0 (a still-full bucket), while the concurrency=2/4 runs' first calls already show ~11.7s waits (a partially-depleted bucket carried over from the prior run) - this is a plausible, not confirmed, confound, disclosed honestly rather than asserted as a definitive explanation).

MEDIUM.note: Essentially no difference (well under 1%) across all 3 concurrency levels.

rate_limiter_mechanism_finding.observation: Per-call rate_limit_wait_ms telemetry (captured directly from grounding_eval.judge's own evaluator_metadata, not inferred) shows that under concurrency=2 and concurrency=4, individual threads' wait times STACK ADDITIVELY (e.g. SMALL concurrency=4's 4 calls show rate_limit_wait_ms of approximately 11656/23669/35756/47791 - i.e. ~12s/24s/36s/48s), exactly mirroring the same total serialization time as the fully sequential concurrency=1 case, just distributed differently across threads.
rate_limiter_mechanism_finding.explanation: utils.rate_limiter.TokenBucket's capacity=1 for the Cerebras key means only ONE token is EVER available at a time, regardless of how many threads are waiting - the shared limiter fully serializes actual provider dispatch under this configuration. Bounded concurrency at the SCHEDULING layer cannot reduce wall-clock time when the binding constraint is a capacity=1 rate limiter, because there is structurally no way for more than one real provider call to be in flight at once - concurrency only changes WHICH thread is waiting, never HOW LONG the total waiting is.
rate_limiter_mechanism_finding.no_burst_confirmed: Zero evidence of any burst above the configured 5 RPM allowance at any concurrency level - every one of the 45 calls' rate_limit_wait_ms values is consistent with strict ~12s minimum spacing, confirming the limiter was not bypassed.
rate_limiter_mechanism_finding.verdict: The rate limiter behaved correctly and was not bypassed under concurrency. This is precisely why concurrency=2/4 show no meaningful speedup (MEDIUM/LARGE) or even a slight apparent regression (SMALL, likely bucket-state-carryover confounded) - the scheduling change is safe but does not help under the CURRENT 5 RPM/capacity=1 rate-limit configuration.

candidate_selection.reason: No candidate (2 or 4) demonstrated a meaningful, defensible latency improvement over concurrency=1. MEDIUM and LARGE fixtures show the wall-clock time is effectively identical (<1% difference, within measurement noise) regardless of concurrency setting, because the shared Cerebras rate limiter's capacity=1 bucket fully serializes actual provider dispatch regardless of how many worker threads are waiting - there is structurally no wall-clock benefit available to capture under the CURRENT 5 RPM/capacity=1 rate-limit configuration. SMALL's apparent 32% regression under concurrency=2/4 is not attributed to a genuine concurrency-caused slowdown (disclosed as plausibly confounded by rate-limiter bucket-state carryover between sequential runs sharing one process-wide limiter instance, with n=1 per condition insufficient to distinguish this from a real effect) - but even setting that result aside entirely, MEDIUM and LARGE's null results alone are sufficient to conclude that no meaningful, defensible latency improvement was demonstrated. Per the governing directive's own explicit instruction: 'If neither 2 nor 4 demonstrates a meaningful defensible improvement: keep 1.' This is a mechanical, capacity=1-driven ceiling, not a flaw in the concurrency implementation itself (which remains correct, tested, and available for use if the rate-limit configuration is ever revisited in a future, separately-authorized pass).

e2e_confirmation.reason: Step 9's candidate selection is KEEP 1 (no change from the current production default, GAP_ANALYSIS_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1). Step 10's E2E comparison is baseline-vs-selected-candidate; since the selected candidate IS the baseline, a live end-to-end comparison would compare GAP_ANALYSIS_MAX_CONCURRENCY=1 against itself, providing zero additional information at the cost of additional live provider traffic. Per the governing directive's own 'keep total live traffic within a reasonable bounded number' instruction and 'do not make hidden exploratory live runs' rule, this redundant comparison was deliberately NOT run - this is a documented decision, not an omission.

production_default_decision.why: Live evidence (this benchmark) did not demonstrate a meaningful, defensible latency improvement from raising GAP_ANALYSIS_MAX_CONCURRENCY above 1 under the current Cerebras 5 RPM/capacity=1 rate-limit configuration - the mechanism is structurally rate-limiter-bound, not scheduling-bound, at this rate. Per Step 11's explicit instruction ('If the evidence does not justify changing it: leave default = 1'), the default remains 1. The bounded-concurrency mechanism itself remains implemented, tested, and available (not removed) for a future pass IF the rate-limit configuration is ever revisited - changing the rate limiter is explicitly out of this pass's scope.
